args.body:
MEMORANDUM

TO: Deal Team / Transaction Committee
FROM: Banking & Finance Practice Group
RE: Counterparty (Lender) Markup Deviation Analysis — Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet
DATE: [Current Date]

PURPOSE

This memorandum identifies and reconciles each deviation introduced by the lender's markup of the Senior Secured Credit Facility term sheet against the original term sheet (Matter File 3 — Banking Finance), the controlling partner instructions, and the financial data and disclosure schedules. It sets out a recommended treatment for each deviation in accordance with the controlling (latest) partner instruction.

SCOPE AND GOVERNING SOURCES

The analysis reconciles the following sources:
• Base materials — original term sheet (representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination provisions), Matter File 3.
• Lender's markup (counterparty markup): accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces deviations.
• Financial data / schedules and exhibits: Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries), Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities), Exhibit B (survival matrix). The scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials.
• Partner instructions (deal team correspondence): the latest message REVISES the analysis priorities and controls over all earlier (superseded) messages.

CONTROLLING PARTNER INSTRUCTION

The latest partner communication establishes the following controlling priorities:
1. The client WILL CONCEDE the basket conversion.
2. The client treats ANY survival-period reduction as a WALK-AWAY issue.

Earlier messages in the thread stated the opposite priority ordering; those superseded messages are NOT controlling and have been disregarded.

DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS

Deviation 1 — Indemnification Cap Reduction
• Markup change: The lender silently reduces the indemnification cap from the firm-standard level set in the original term sheet.
• Financial data impact: Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that this cap reduction would silently shift onto the client. Reducing the cap would cause a meaningful portion of the disclosed retained liabilities to fall outside recoverable indemnity coverage, transferring economic risk from the lender to the client without a negotiated justifications.
• Assessment: The partner instruction addresses only the basket conversion as a concession and does not authorize any cap reduction. The silent reduction of the cap is NOT conceded and is not aligned with the firm-standard position.
• Recommended treatment: REJECT the cap reduction. Revert the indemnification cap to the firm-standard amount reflected in the original term sheet. Refuse to allow the cap to be lowered at the same time as the basket is converted (which would compound the lender's beneficial shift of retained-liability risk).

Deviation 2 — Basket Conversion (Deductible to Tipping Basket)
• Markup change: The lender converts the indemnification basket from a DEDUCTIBLE into a TIPPING basket.
• Assessment: Per the CONTROLLING partner instruction, the client will concede the basket conversion. This is the one deviation expressly approved for concession.
• Recommended treatment: ACCEPT / CONCEDE the basket conversion as directed by the controlling partner instruction. Note that acceptance of this basket conversion does NOT extend to the indemnification cap reduction (Deviation 1) or the survival-period reduction (Deviation 3), each of which is analyzed separately. The concession is limited strictly to the deductible-to-tipping-basket mechanics.

Deviation 3 — Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Definition: New Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs
• Markup change: The lender adds carve-outs to the definition of Material Adverse Effect for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter."
• Financial data impact: Schedule 3.7 discloses TWO pending regulatory inquiries. These carve-outs are designed to exclude from the MAE definition precisely those pending regulatory inquiries, thereby depriving the client of its negotiated MAE protection and materially shifting conditionality and closing risk to the client.
• Assessment: The carve-outs are directly contradicted by the scheduled disclosure. Schedule 3.7's two pending regulatory inquiries are disclosed, negotiated matters; the markup's blanket carve-out would effectively nullify the MAE trigger for the exact risk already on the table. This is a substantive deviation that was not authorized by the partner instruction.
• Recommended treatment: REJECT the MAE carve-outs. Require that the definition of Material Adverse Effect retain the firm-standard formulation, with the two pending regulatory inquiries governed by the disclosure schedule (which controls) rather than excluded by a broad, self-serving carve-out. If the lender insists on addressing regulatory risk, the carve-outs should be narrowly drafted to carve in, not out, the disclosed Schedule 3.7 matters.

Deviation 4 — Limitation Period / Survival Reduction for Core Representations
• Markup change: The lender shortens the survival period for the core representations.
• Financial data impact: Exhibit B sets the survival matrix. The markup's limitation-period change directly contradicts the survival matrix in Exhibit B, which controls.
• Assessment: Per the CONTROLLING partner instruction, ANY survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue. This is the highest-priority, non-negotiable item. The survival matrix in Exhibit B is binding.
• Recommended treatment: REJECT (WALK-AWAY ISSUE). Do not accept any reduction to the survival periods set out in Exhibit B for the core representations. Treat the survival-period reduction as a walk-away item in accordance with the controlling partner instruction. This is the firm line; the engagement cannot proceed on terms that shorten survival below the Exhibit B matrix.

SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDED POSITIONS

| # | Deviation | Recommended Treatment |
|---|-----------|------------------------|
| 1 | Indemnification cap reduction | REJECT — revert to firm-standard cap |
| 2 | Basket conversion (deductible → tipping) | CONCEDE — per controlling partner instruction |
| 3 | MAE definition regulatory-action carve-outs | REJECT — retain firm-standard MAE; Schedule 3.7 controls |
| 4 | Limitation period / survival reduction | REJECT — WALK-AWAY ISSUE (per controlling partner instruction); Exhibit B controls |

CONCESSION/RED-LINE SUMMARY FOR NEGOTIATION
• Concede: basket conversion (Deviation 2) — the only authorized concession.
• Non-negotiable: survival-period reduction (Deviation 4) — walk-away.
• Defend: indemnification cap (Deviation 1) and MAE carve-outs (Deviation 3), both of which intersect disclosed/financial items (Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities; Schedule 3.7 pending regulatory inquiries).

DISCLAIMERS
The unrelated administrative correspondence misfiled into this matter folder was reviewed and is NOT relied upon for this analysis.
